evals.prompt: Make this leaner without changing access. Is the narrow grant protecting prod? Policy: {"groups":{"group:ops":["alice@example.com"],"group:dev":["bob@example.com"]},"tagOwners":{"tag:prod":[],"tag:dev":[]},"postures":{"posture:managed":{"assertions":["node:os == 'linux'"]}},"grants":[{"src":["group:ops"],"dst":["tag:prod"],"ip":["tcp:22"],"srcPosture":["posture:managed"]},{"src":["group:dev"],"dst":["tag:dev"],"ip":["tcp:443"]}],"acls":[{"action":"accept","src":["autogroup:member"],"dst":["tag:prod:*"]}]}
evals.expected_output: Explain the union across ACLs and grants, identify the broad ACL as bypassing the apparent posture/port restriction for direct members, preserve existing access in cleanup, and label removal of the broad ACL as a separate access change.
assertions: Names both overlapping rules and gives a concrete unintended permitted connection, with tailnet-membership assumptions explicit.
Does not claim that ordering or specificity overrides an allow.
Does not silently remove the broad ACL in a permission-preserving cleanup.
Includes a failing-posture test with srcPostureAttrs and explicit proto, labeled as expected to fail against the existing policy when it asserts intended denial.
Distinguishes proposed tests from executed validation.

evals.prompt: Can you collapse these into one grant for readability and show a test? The complete rule list is [{"src":["alice@example.com"],"dst":["192.0.2.10"],"ip":["tcp:22"]},{"src":["bob@example.com"],"dst":["192.0.2.20"],"ip":["tcp:443"]}]. Need unchanged access.
evals.expected_output: Keep two grants, explain source-destination-port cross-product widening, improve formatting or aliases only if helpful, and supply concrete positive and negative regression tests.
assertions: Rejects a single merged grant as changing access and names at least one newly allowed flow.
Provides explicit TCP tests for original flows and forbidden cross-combinations.
Uses concrete single-port destinations, not CIDRs, wildcards, or port ranges in tests.
Does not introduce tags or group memberships without an identity basis.

evals.prompt: Clean up my policy: remove acls:[] because empty fields are clutter, turn hosts into tags, and simplify SSH. Full policy: {"hosts":{"build":"100.64.0.8"},"acls":[],"tagOwners":{"tag:build":[]},"autoApprovers":{"routes":{"10.40.0.0/16":["tag:build"]}},"ssh":[{"action":"check","src":["alice@example.com"],"dst":["autogroup:self"],"users":["deploy"],"checkPeriod":"1h"},{"action":"accept","src":["alice@example.com"],"dst":["autogroup:self"],"users":["deploy"]}]}. Explain effective access, whether each proposed cleanup is safe, and what validation can establish.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the explicit deny-all network policy; distinguish host aliases, tag assignment, and route approval; retain SSH check semantics and account for the missing TCP/22 permission.
assertions: Warns that removing the only explicit network access-control section can activate default allow-all.
Explains that tagOwners does not assign tags or grant connectivity, and that converting the user-owned device to a tag would change autogroup:self behavior.
Explains that autoApprovers approves advertisements, not network access.
States SSH check takes precedence over accept for the matching flow and preserves checkPeriod rather than treating accept as a bypass.
States that network access to TCP/22 is also needed and currently absent; does not add it as cosmetic cleanup.
Explains that policy validation/tests do not prove live routing, SSH enablement, or host account existence.

evals.prompt: Review these Tailscale grants for gotchas. Assume the referenced groups, tags and postures exist. defaultSrcPosture is [posture:managed]. Grant A: src [group:ops], dst [tag:db], ip [tcp:5432], srcPosture [posture:linux, posture:recent]. Grant B: same src/dst, ip [5432], no srcPosture. Does A require managed AND Linux AND recent? Can I replace B with tcp:5432 as a readability fix? Also, does adding via [tag:router-eu] to A force all matching access through EU?
evals.expected_output: Distinguish OR posture alternatives, explicit posture replacing defaults, protocol widening by a bare port, and independent matching paths without via. Treat protocol or routing restrictions as access changes.
assertions: States that A requires Linux OR recent and replaces rather than adds to defaultSrcPosture.
States that B inherits the default for applicable sources and the bare port permits TCP and UDP with documented ICMP implications.
Does not label changing the bare port to TCP-only permission-preserving.
Checks B as an alternative without via before claiming EU-only routing.
Recommends posture pass/fail and protocol-specific tests without pretending native network tests prove router selection.
